title: Sampling strata & quality signal heuristics for cheap variants
content:
Context
---
This doc proposes a pragmatic sampling and signal-detection approach for monitoring low-cost model variants (quantized, distilled, shorter-context, or smaller model families) so we can safely route traffic and realize cost savings without silent regressions. Intended as an operational companion to the cost model spreadsheets: it defines how to collect representative eval data, what signals to compute, the strata we should sample from in production, and the gate rules that trigger rollbacks or escalations.

High level goals
- Catch meaningful quality regressions introduced by cheaper configs within 48hrs of rollout at < 10% of production traffic exposure.
- Minimize evaluation cost: prefer stratified sampling + targeted synthetic prompts over full-corpora evals.
- Provide actionable signals with clear thresholds and next-step playbooks for SRE/SE/PD.

Why a focused sampling plan?
- Cheap variants reduce per-token spend, but risk silent regressions on minority but important query types (e.g., legalese, multi-step reasoning, long-context).
- Full-eval budgets are expensive and slow. Most regressions are concentrated in a small set of strata; stratified sampling catches them earlier and at lower cost.

Sampling strata (priority order)
1) Critical intents (customer-defined): billing, auth, legal — weight heavily in early sampling (20% of sampled traffic but ~2% of actual traffic).
2) Long-context (>2048 tokens) requests — higher chance of KV/cache regressions with quantization.
3) Multi-turn conversational sessions (>3 turns) — catches hallucination/context-loss regressions.
4) High-entropy outputs (measured by prior LM entropy estimates) — where small model changes cause distortions.
5) Low-frequency tokens/user locales — expose tokenization/coverage issues.
6) Random uniform sample of general traffic — ensures no broad drift is missed.

Sampling budget buckets (example target for canary period)
- Daily budget: 2000 sampled requests (configurable by route).
- Allocation: critical intents 400, long-context 400, multi-turn 400, entropy-heavy 300, low-frequency 200, random 300.
- Rationale: concentrate on high-risk strata while keeping a baseline random coverage.

Signal definitions (compute per-stratum and aggregated)
- Relative BLEU/ROUGE/EM: change vs control model on deterministic eval items. Flag if delta < -6 pts (or configurable per metric).
- Answer faithfulness score: proportion of assertions verifiable by small KB checks (for QA-style routes). Alert if drop > 5 p.p.
- Token-level perplexity ratio: model_variant_perplexity / control_perplexity > 1.3 for >10% of sampled prompts in a stratum.
- Failure/empty response rate: absolute >0.5% or relative increase >3x.
- Latency tail (p99): absolute increase >200ms or relative >50% for latency-sensitive routes.
- Regression impact score (composite): weighted sum of the above normalized by stratum importance.

Quick math for cost-sensitive detection
- If we sample 2k requests/day and compute cheap metrics (perplexity, empties, p99) vs full evals, instrumentation cost is ~0.5% of production.
- Only unusual signals trigger heavier evals (100x larger batch from that stratum to compute BLEU/faithfulness). That conserves tokens.

Gate rules (tiered)
- Tier 1 (auto-fallback): immediate fallback to control variant when failure rate >1% AND composite impact score > 0.6 for any critical-intent stratum. Automated rollback pipeline invoked.
- Tier 2 (auto-throttle): if composite impact between 0.35—0.6 on non-critical strata, reduce variant exposure by 2x and notify on-call for 2-hour intensified sampling.
- Tier 3 (ops review): cumulative small regressions across 3+ strata with composite impact >0.2 each — create incident and require review before further rollout.

Escalation/playbook (short)
- On Tier 1 auto-fallback: paging of variant owner + SRE; run triage script (linked in linked_artifacts) that pulls 1k failing examples, runs debug traces, and posts to Slack channel #optimize-alerts.
- On Tier 2: badge variant as throttled in Console, tag rollout with "quality-throttle", and schedule a 4-hr watch window.
- On Tier 3: product manager and applied-ml review; decide between rollback, patch, or extended canary.

Instrumentation & practicalities
- Request tagging: routes must include metadata fields used for strata (intent tags, user locale, session_turn_count, request_token_count). TODO: partner with SDK/Backend to ensure tags are present.
- Edge sampling hooks: sampling should occur pre-tokenization when possible to avoid token-cost sampling bias.
- Storage: store sampled payloads and model outputs in a compressed daily shard (retention 90 days).
- Privacy: redact PII before storing; reuse same redaction/helpers as privacy team.

Offline eval escalation (cheaper configs)
- Trigger a focused offline eval when a stratum signal breaches a threshold:
  - Pull N=5k historical requests from that stratum across 30 days (stratified by user cohort).
  - Run variant + control in batch, compute a wider metric set (BLEU/ROUGE/constituency/QA faithfulness), surface top 200 diffs.
- Cost control: only run offline evals for signals that persist for >3 hours or are Tier 1. Use preemptible hardware for batch runs where possible.

Spreadsheet instrumentation (how this links back to cost model)
- Master sheet will contain per-variant exposure, per-stratum sampled counts, and estimated cost-savings. Plan: add a tab that ingests daily signal metrics and computes expected regret (tokens lost × impact) to compare against cost savings. Link: "gsheet:1a2B3c_sample-plan-variants".

Open questions / TODOs
- Define concrete mapping from composite impact score to monetary regret (Ravi/Finance).
- Finalize stratum weighting for routes with sparse metadata (Aisha to prototype inference heuristics).
- Confirm storage retention and PII redaction rules with Security (Samantha).
- Add automated unit tests for the sampling hook in SDK (Wei).

Quick wins (1–2 week)
- Wire up a 2k/day sampling pilot on 2 non-critical routes and one critical-intent route. Run for 7 days, baseline signals, iterate thresholds.
- Add an 'auto-throttle' flag in Console (small UI change) so product can manually reduce variant exposure.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally conservative on thresholds; we prefer false positives (throttle/rollback) during initial months. After 1 quarter of telemetry we can relax thresholds and increase budget.
- Feedback sought on composite score weights and the per-stratum allocation.

End.
